summary: Slug-level hard flock claim lock (plan-claim.sh over sink-lock.sh) preventing two Claude sessions from double-working the same /z-plan or /z-audit-plan slug; orthogonal to the advisory active-plan-registry. As of skill-overhaul-phase1, /z-plan delegates acquisition to scripts/z-preflight.sh (which resolves stale-takeover silently) while /z-audit-plan still calls plan-claim.sh directly with the original interactive default-abort stale-takeover gate.

entry_points.summary: Refresh TTL and detect lost claim; exit 0=ok/transient-error, 9=confirmed-lost
Release lock best-effort using --expected-holder guard; always exit 0
Read-only stale classification via sink-lock check-stale; never mutates; exit 0=held,1=free,2=stale,3=corrupt
Low-level flock+daemon+TTL primitive; plan-claim.sh delegates all flock mechanics to it

invariants: The lockless awareness registry (active-plan-registry.py) stays ADVISORY. The claim lock is a SEPARATE hard lock. Claim acquire/heartbeat/release MUST NEVER write a peer's registry record. The registry's overlap output is NEVER a hard gate. (Invariant 1)

Claim acquire is the FIRST action after slug+run-id resolution — before run-brief init, before register, before any artifact write. Holds for both direct callers (/z-audit-plan) and preflight-delegated callers (/z-plan, where it is step 4 of scripts/z-preflight.sh's fixed sequence, before register at step 5). (Invariant 2)
No reliance on a cross-call EXIT trap. Hard-kill recovery is guaranteed only by release on every halt-finalize path + sink-lock TTL stale-takeover. (Invariant 3)

Contention/takeover handling is now caller-dependent (skill-overhaul-phase1, LEDGER T106). plan-claim.sh acquire itself is unchanged and still NON-INTERACTIVE (never calls AskUserQuestion; decisions belong entirely to the caller). Two caller paths currently coexist: (a) skills delegating acquisition to scripts/z-preflight.sh (currently /z-plan, no --no-claim) — the wrapper resolves acquire rc==2 (stale-takeover) SILENTLY: CLAIM_HELD=1, no ask, a NOTE: line to stderr only (refusing the already-completed OS-level takeover would just release it right back for no benefit); live-peer contention (rc==1) and corrupt lock (rc==3) are HARD STOPS inside the wrapper (exit 10 / exit 11 respectively) that the calling skill still resolves interactively (or via Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1 when unattended) around the non-zero preflight exit code. (b) skills still calling plan-claim.sh directly (currently /z-audit-plan, not yet migrated) — retain the ORIGINAL interactive AskUserQuestion menu on all three non-zero branches, including a default-ABORT stale-takeover gate (rc==2). Read-only skills (/z-stats, /z-explore, /z-audit) pass --no-claim to scripts/z-preflight.sh, skipping claim acquisition entirely (CLAIM_HELD unconditionally 0; contention/corrupt exits cannot occur). Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1 remains the explicit unattended opt-in on the direct-call path; Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1 skips claiming entirely on ALL paths. (Invariant 4)
Holder string is the only carrier of identity: <session>::<run>::<command>. Colon in any field is rejected (exit 2) to preserve '::' delimiter unambiguity. (Invariant 6)

Session id is export-once AND persisted to archive/$RUN/session-id; restored on resume before every acquire call. plan-claim.sh never calls session-id itself (whether invoked directly or via scripts/z-preflight.sh, which follows the same persist/restore rule internally). (Invariant 7)
Cross-plan (Hermes) acquires plan-claim locks in sorted ascending slug order to guarantee deadlock-freedom. (INV-6 in hermes-orchestration)

reap-stale is strictly read-only: it never acquires, releases, or kills. Callers (z-reconcile) must independently confirm the daemon PID is dead before removing a lock file, even when reap-stale reports 'stale'.

acquire.0: acquired, self-reentry, or Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1 — caller holds the lock (or disabled)
acquire.1: live-peer contention — holder JSON printed to stdout (best-effort, TOCTOU, display-only); caller does NOT hold lock. Under scripts/z-preflight.sh delegation this becomes a wrapper-level hard stop (exit 10) for the calling skill to resolve.
acquire.2: stale-takeover succeeded — caller NOW holds the lock; normal post-crash path. Resolved SILENTLY (proceed, CLAIM_HELD=1) when acquired via scripts/z-preflight.sh; resolved via an interactive default-ABORT AskUserQuestion when acquired directly (e.g. current /z-audit-plan).
acquire.3: corrupt lock or invalid-holder/invalid-args — caller does NOT hold lock. Under scripts/z-preflight.sh delegation this becomes a wrapper-level hard stop (exit 11).

heartbeat.0: refreshed, disabled, OR transient read error (heartbeat_error emitted, non-fatal)
heartbeat.9: confirmed lost claim — holder present-and-different or lock free; transient read failure is NOT exit 9

release.0: always (best-effort; --expected-holder guard prevents releasing a peer's lock)

reap-stale.0: held — lock is live and held by a live process
reap-stale.1: free — no lock file or empty
reap-stale.2: stale — lock held by a dead PID or expired heartbeat

preflight_wrapper.note: Not itself part of this concept's source_file set (documented by its own script header); recorded here because it is now the primary caller of plan-claim.sh acquire for /z-plan and changes the observable contention/takeover UX for that caller only.
preflight_wrapper.sequence_position: step 4 of 8 (resolve -> session-id -> RUN-stamp -> claim -> register -> run-brief-init -> run_start -> kernel-resolve)

claim_branch_policy.acquire_rc_2_stale_takeover: CLAIM_HELD=1, proceed SILENTLY (no AskUserQuestion; NOTE: line to stderr only)
claim_branch_policy.acquire_rc_1_live_peer: wrapper HARD STOPS at exit 10 (holder JSON to stderr); calling skill resolves interactively around the non-zero exit
claim_branch_policy.acquire_rc_3_corrupt: wrapper HARD STOPS at exit 11; calling skill resolves interactively around the non-zero exit
claim_branch_policy.no_claim_flag: claim step (4) skipped entirely; CLAIM_HELD unconditionally 0; used by read-only skills (/z-stats, /z-explore, /z-audit)

not_yet_migrated_callers: z-audit-plan (calls plan-claim.sh directly; gates on CLAIM_RC, not CLAIM_HELD; retains full interactive contention/stale-takeover/corrupt menu with default-ABORT stale-takeover)

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_TTL_SECS.description: TTL seconds for claim liveness. Not a TOML key. Not emitted by export-env.

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE.description: Set to 1 to allow unattended runs to proceed through contention/stale-takeover/corrupt without aborting. Meaningful on the direct-call path (/z-audit-plan) for all three branches; on the scripts/z-preflight.sh-delegated path (/z-plan) it is only relevant to the wrapper's hard-stop branches (contention rc==1, corrupt rc==3) since stale-takeover (rc==2) already proceeds unconditionally under that wrapper.

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE.description: Set to 1 to skip all claim locking. Every subcommand is an immediate exit-0 no-op. Release is a safe no-op regardless of event presence. Applies identically on both the direct-call and scripts/z-preflight.sh-delegated paths; distinct from --no-claim (a z-preflight.sh-only flag that skips its own claim step).

gotchas: exit-2 (stale-takeover) is the NORMAL post-crash recovery path, not a rare edge case. The setsid-detached daemon survives SIGKILL and leaks until TTL. On the direct-call path (/z-audit-plan) the unattended default is: abort unless Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE=1. On the scripts/z-preflight.sh-delegated path (/z-plan) there is no abort option for this branch at all — it always proceeds (CLAIM_HELD=1), attended or unattended.

/z-plan and /z-audit-plan currently diverge on stale-takeover UX: /z-plan (via scripts/z-preflight.sh) resolves it silently and proceeds; /z-audit-plan (direct plan-claim.sh call) still shows an interactive default-ABORT AskUserQuestion. This is a real, current inconsistency in the codebase (skill-overhaul-phase1, uncommitted), not a doc error.

CLAIM_HELD is only meaningful for scripts/z-preflight.sh-delegated callers (currently /z-plan); it is exported automatically by the wrapper's fixed output contract. /z-audit-plan never sets or reads CLAIM_HELD — it gates everything on CLAIM_RC directly, and a missing CLAIM_RC assignment there has the same lock-leak failure mode a missing CLAIM_HELD assignment has in /z-plan.
The holder JSON printed by acquire (exit 1/2) and status is best-effort TOCTOU — re-read AFTER sink-lock returned. The gate keys on the exit code, not the JSON. Do not gate logic on JSON content.

Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE=1: release is a safe no-op and is NOT gated on an acquire event being present. Callers always safe to call release regardless of this knob. Distinct from --no-claim, which is a scripts/z-preflight.sh-only flag (not a plan-claim.sh knob) that skips the wrapper's own claim step for read-only skills.

heartbeat exit 9 fires ONLY on confirmed ownership change (holder present-and-different, or lock free). A transient read/corrupt error is heartbeat_error + exit 0 (non-fatal). Do not conflate these two paths.

heartbeat BEFORE every AskUserQuestion is the load-bearing call — it extends TTL to survive the user-wait. The after-gate heartbeat (user_wait_end) is optional when the next phase heartbeat is imminent.

At exit-2 abort (stale-takeover, we hold the lock), release MUST be called before aborting. At exit-0/1/3 abort, do NOT call release (we never held the lock). This applies to the direct-call path (/z-audit-plan); the scripts/z-preflight.sh-delegated path (/z-plan) has no abort branch for exit-2.

session-id persist+restore (Invariant 7) is required for the self-reentry guard to work on macOS. Without it, a resumed run sees its own prior claim as a foreign contender. Applies identically whether plan-claim.sh is invoked directly or via scripts/z-preflight.sh.
Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_TTL_SECS, Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_OVERRIDE, and Z_HARNESS_CLAIM_DISABLE are env-only. They are NOT in config.py DEFAULTS or VALIDATORS and are NOT emitted by export-env.

plan-claim.sh must pass --ttl-seconds to sink-lock read-holder so the stale flag is consistent with the TTL acquire uses. Omitting it causes read-holder to use sink-lock's default (7200), which can report stale:false for a slug that acquire would actually take over (2700 basis).

--no-claim (scripts/z-preflight.sh flag, read-only skills: /z-stats, /z-explore, /z-audit) skips claim step 4 entirely — plan-claim.sh acquire is never invoked; CLAIM_HELD is unconditionally 0; contention (exit 10) and corrupt-lock (exit 11) exits cannot occur under this flag since claiming never runs.

z-audit-plan fires an early heartbeat before the slug-select AskUserQuestion even before the claim gate fully resolves — only if CLAIM_RC==0 at that point (CLAIM_RC, not CLAIM_HELD, since z-audit-plan never delegates to scripts/z-preflight.sh). This is distinct from the main phase-boundary heartbeat cadence.
Hermes cross-plan acquires claim locks in sorted ascending slug order (deadlock-free). Any new cross-plan callers must follow the same ordering invariant.

commands/z-plan.md and commands/z-audit-plan.md no longer exist in this repo (commands/ was retired in the 2026-06-20 skills-atom re-flip). The caller-side wiring is exclusively in skills/z-plan/SKILL.md and skills/z-audit-plan/SKILL.md; any doc or memory referencing the old commands/ paths is stale.

reap-stale is a distinct, purely read-only subcommand (not part of the acquire/heartbeat/release triad). It is consumed by z-reconcile for workspace-audit lock classification and must never be used to justify an automatic rm — a lock with a live daemon PID must never be removed regardless of reap-stale's reported state.

sink-lock.sh's holder daemon now blocks SIGTERM/SIGHUP (pthread_sigmask) around both lock-content critical sections (write on startup, zero on signal-handler exit) to prevent a self-deadlock re-entrant-flock race found under load stress (T118). Internal robustness fix only — plan-claim.sh's exit codes/events/holder-JSON are unchanged. See docs/llm/lock-signal-safety.json.
